title: Trump: The White House takes over CDC website, changes COVID-19 guidance
description_short: Trump: The White House takes over CDC website, changes COVID-19 guidance
description_medium: Updated CDC coronavirus guidance appeared online on September 18, 2020, and was removed three days later. The supplied account says it covered airborne transmission and testing advice. The CDC called it an unpublished draft posted in error; an unnamed official reportedly attributed the removal to White House interference, leaving the reason disputed.
description_long: Updated CDC guidance on coronavirus transmission and testing appeared on the agency’s website on September 18, 2020, then disappeared three days later. The supplied account says the page discussed airborne transmission and advice for people exposed to the virus. The CDC said an unpublished draft had been posted in error. A different explanation, attributed in the packet to an unnamed official through attorney Jonathan Perkins, was that the White House had interfered. Those accounts leave the central question unresolved: the record describes a rapid publication and removal and conflicting explanations, but does not show who changed the page or establish that the White House took control of the CDC website. The dispute matters because the change concerned public-health guidance during the pandemic, when clinicians and the public relied on CDC communications. The linked timeline returned an empty HTTP 202 response, so the official statements and reporting behind the competing accounts could not be checked here.
notes: The linked timeline returned HTTP 202 with an empty response. The supplied draft describes competing explanations for the page's removal but does not establish a White House takeover or identify who changed the guidance.

title: Donald Trump refuses to concede, promises court battle
description_short: Donald Trump refuses to concede, promises court battle
description_medium: Donald Trump refuses to concede, promises court battle. Donald Trump, the first president since 1992 to not win re-election, refuses to concede and promises to battle the election in court. Sources https://www.usnews.com/news/politics/articles/2020-11-07/text-of-statement-from-president-donald-trump https://www.donaldjtrump.com/media/statement-from-president-donald-j.-trump/ Photo: Duncan C This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, legal development, documented relationship, or policy consequence linked directly or indirectly to Trump. The downstream effects include institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and accountability pressure across affected systems.
description_long: On November 7, 2020, after the presidential race was called for Joe Biden, Donald Trump said he would not concede and promised to challenge the result in court. The statement came as election officials continued counting ballots and state results were being finalized. Refusing to concede did not itself change the certified vote totals, but it signaled a prolonged public dispute over the outcome. Trump’s statement announced legal challenges without specifying in the supplied account which cases would be filed or what evidence they would present. That distinction is important: a candidate may contest an election through the courts, while claims about fraud or the validity of results require evidence and judicial review. The provided material documents Trump’s public refusal and promise of litigation, but does not give case filings, court responses, or the later course of those challenges. Those records would be needed for a fuller account of the legal effort and its consequences.

title: Trump: Special Counsel reports that Trump adviser violated the Hatch Act
description_short: Trump: Special Counsel reports that Trump adviser violated the Hatch Act
description_medium: Special Counsel Henry J. Kerner reported that Trump adviser Peter Navarro violated the Hatch Act by making political attacks on Joe Biden and Kamala Harris while serving in government. The law restricts partisan political activity by federal employees. The supplied account does not identify later discipline or a response from Trump.
description_long: Special Counsel Henry J. Kerner reported that Trump adviser Peter Navarro violated the Hatch Act through political attacks on Joe Biden and Kamala Harris while Navarro served in a government role. The Hatch Act restricts partisan political activity by federal employees, including using official authority for electoral purposes. Kerner’s report was an administrative ethics finding, not a criminal conviction. It placed a finding about a senior adviser before President Donald Trump, but the supplied material does not say how the White House responded or whether Navarro faced any discipline. The record also omits the exact statements, their dates, and the full report’s reasoning. Those details would clarify the conduct covered by the finding and its consequences. The event can be described as a watchdog’s reported Hatch Act violation; the limited account does not show that Trump directed Navarro’s conduct or explain what action followed the report.
